segments.visual: The code panel holds four lines; the shelf holds the cast scaled ten thousand times, about a million rows, as four files. Beside each line, a counter: rows read.

sentences.text: You've seen it happen: a few lines of PySpark come back instantly, and then one line takes minutes.
Here are four lines, run on our cast scaled up to about a million rows.

segments.visual: The counters fill as each line runs: 0, 0, 0, then 1,030,000 for the fourth.

sentences.text: The first three read nothing. Not one row.
The fourth reads every single row. So why do the first three read nothing?

segments.visual: Series wordmark, Spark, Visually; Part I, How Spark runs a job; the episode title.

sentences.text: Welcome to Spark, Visually.
Today: nothing happens until you ask.

segments.visual: Back to the home shot and the cast's four files; the benches stay empty. Line 1 types; a box, filter, appears on the driver desk. Nothing moves.

sentences.text: Back to our 103 patients. Line one filters them down to the higher-risk patients. Or rather, it writes that down.
sentences.say: Back to our hundred and three patients. Line one filters them down to the higher-risk patients. Or rather, it writes that down.

sentences.text: A step is added to a plan: filter. Not one row moves.

segments.visual: Lines 2 and 3 type; two more boxes join the chain: new column, select. The rows-read counter stays at 0.

sentences.text: Line two adds a column, and line three keeps just two columns. Each one adds a step.
Three lines, and not a single row has been read.

segments.visual: A card: a DataFrame is a recipe, its source and its steps.

sentences.text: A DataFrame isn't a table of rows. It's a recipe: where the rows come from, and the steps to follow.

segments.visual: Line 4 glows: hi.count(). Four tasks drop from the driver to the benches, one per file.

sentences.text: Line four asks a question: how many rows are left? That's an action, and an action runs the recipe.
The driver sends 4 tasks down, one per file.
sentences.say: The driver sends four tasks down, one per file.

segments.visual: Each bench reads its file; its chips pass a filter gate as they arrive, in one stream, and the chips without a risk ring drop away. The new-column and select boxes stay dark; only the x column leaves the shelf.

sentences.text: Each task reads its file and filters the rows as they arrive, in a single pass.
And the new column? A count doesn't need it, so Spark never computes it. It even reads just the one column the filter needs.

segments.visual: 46 chips remain; four partial counts go to one final task; 46 rises to the driver.

sentences.text: 46 higher-risk patients make it through, and one number goes up to the driver: 46.
sentences.say: Forty-six higher-risk patients make it through, and one number goes up to the driver: forty-six.

segments.visual: The trays are empty again. Line 5 glows: hi.show(). One task reads the first file, then a second task the next, and it stops there: show() needs only 21 rows. This time the chips pass all three steps in one stream: the filter, the new column stamped on, the risk ring dropped by select. Rows print in the code panel.

sentences.text: Line five asks to see the rows. Another action, so the recipe runs again, from the files.
This time it needs every step, and it still makes one pass: filter, add the column, keep two.

segments.visual: A card: normally, every action starts from storage; keeping a result is a promise for Episode 10.

sentences.text: Spark didn't keep the count's work. Normally, every action starts again from storage, unless you ask Spark to keep a result.
And even that request waits for an action. That's episode 10.
sentences.say: And even that request waits for an action. That's episode ten.

segments.visual: The whole chain on the driver desk lights at once.

sentences.text: So why be lazy? Because when the action arrives, Spark sees the whole recipe at once, and can plan it.
Here's our cast again, written with its files sorted by risk.

segments.visual: A copy of the filter box slides down into the read; the filter stays on the desk. All four tasks run: the two files holding no higher-risk patients grey out and are skipped, and their tasks read nothing; a counter: rows read, 53 instead of 103.

sentences.text: Spark pushes the filter into the read itself. Files that hold no higher-risk patients are skipped, and it reads 53 rows instead of 103.
sentences.say: Spark pushes the filter into the read itself. Files that hold no higher-risk patients are skipped, and it reads fifty-three rows instead of a hundred and three.

sentences.text: Episode 6 shows how.

segments.visual: A sorting card: transformations (filter, withColumn, select) hand back a DataFrame; actions (count, show, collect, write) hand back a number, rows, or files.

sentences.text: So, two kinds of line. A transformation hands back a new DataFrame: a longer recipe, and no work.
An action hands back a result: a number, rows on screen or in your hands, or files written. Actions do the work.

segments.visual: A CSV file on the shelf: with inferSchema, two jobs run to look at the data; with a schema given, none. Beneath: reading Parquet or JSON by path runs 1 job, for the schema; over Spark Connect these jobs wait until the schema is first needed.

sentences.text: A common exception: read a CSV file and ask Spark to guess its column types, and it runs 2 jobs, to look at the data.
sentences.say: A common exception: read a CSV file and ask Spark to guess its column types, and it runs two jobs, to look at the data.

sentences.text: Give it the schema, and the read is lazy again.

segments.visual: Three recap cards: transformations write the recipe; actions run it, one pass per pile; normally, every action starts from storage.

sentences.text: Let's gather it up.
Transformations write the recipe. Actions run it, in one pass over each pile.
And normally, every action starts again from storage.

segments.visual: The count's job and stage tally: 2 jobs, 2 stages. Next episode title: Cut at the walls.

sentences.text: One loose end: our count was one action, yet Spark ran it as 2 jobs and 2 stages.
sentences.say: One loose end: our count was one action, yet Spark ran it as two jobs and two stages.

sentences.text: How does Spark cut up the work? Next time: cut at the walls.

segments.visual: Series end card with the next episode title.

sentences.text: This has been Spark, Visually. Thanks for watching the cluster with us.
